```plato
//==
// # TimeVaryingValues — derived functions for ITimeVarying<TValue>
//
// Bodies for the `ITimeVarying<TValue>` interface declared in
// `time-varying.concepts.plato`. A time-varying value is sampled at a `Duration`
// offset from its owner's start via `Sample`; the helpers rename that sampling
// and work over a span given by two boundary Durations. Pure expressions only;
// all inputs are immutable and evaluation is side-effect free. See `README.md`
// for naming and unit conventions.

// The library block is TimeVaryingValues rather than the file stem's TimeVarying:
// that name is already taken by the interface these bodies derive from.
library TimeVaryingValues
{
    //==
    // # ITimeVarying<TValue>
    //
    // A value sampled at a moment in time via Sample(time: Duration). Key times
    // are Duration offsets from the owner's start, so helpers take explicit
    // boundary Durations rather than assuming a clip length.
    //
    // The change/delta helpers subtract two samples, which the type variable
    // $TValue supports by the same duck-typing the interval helpers rely on
    // (IInterval.Extent subtracts two $T). A formal `where TValue: IAdditive`
    // bound on ITimeVarying is deferred: its implementors span motion-graphics.types.plato
    // and future/keyframes.types.plato (AnimationTrack/TangentTrack), which are
    // outside this package's edit scope, so the bound cannot be filled tree-wide here.

    // The sampled value at a time offset; a readable spelling of Sample.
    ValueAt(self: ITimeVarying<$TValue>, time: Duration): $TValue
        => self.Sample(time);
```
